evidence.quote: {{ety|en|id=shining|:bor|fr:brillant<id:shining>|tree=1}} {{bor+|en|fr|brillant}} (late 17th century), present participle of the verb {{m|fr|briller}}, from {{der|en|it|brillare}}, possibly from {{der|en|la|berillus}}, {{m|la|beryllus||a beryl, gem, eyeglass}}, from {{der|en|grc|βήρυλλος||beryl}}. {{surf|en|fr:briller|alt1=brill(er)|-i-|-ant}}.

"sparkling with light or luster," 1680s, from French brilliant "sparkling, shining"… See origin and meaning of brilliant. from French brilliant "sparkling, shining" present participle of briller "to shine" (16c.

proposed_usageNote: This surface form has other senses (light / shine). The usage curve may mix them.
